drivingQuestion: What is Beit Shammai's reasoning for a minimum of one dinar?
outcomeNote: Rabbi Zeira supplies a reason; challenged in the next unit.

segments.he: בְּכֶסֶף, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים בְּדִינָר וְכו׳. מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי? אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: שֶׁכֵּן אִשָּׁה מַקְפֶּדֶת עַל עַצְמָהּ, וְאֵין מִתְקַדֶּשֶׁת בְּפָחוֹת מִדִּינָר.
segments.en: § The Gemara returns to the halakhot of the mishna. The mishna teaches that if one betroths a woman «with money, Beit Shammai say» he must betroth her «with» at least «one dinar,» whereas according to the opinion of Beit Hillel even one peruta is sufficient. The Gemara asks: «What is the reasoning of Beit Shammai? Rabbi Zeira says:» Their reasoning is «that a woman is particular about herself» and considers it beneath her dignity to be acquired with a paltry sum, «and» therefore she «will not» agree to «be betrothed with less than one dinar.»
